commits.author: Codex
commits.original_message:
soc: qcom: spm: use a raw lock for the MSM8226 L2 map

The fixed-range APC transaction runs on CPU0 in a synchronous IPI.
Its SAW reads and writes use the map published by the L2 owner. Setting
fast_io selects a spinlock_t, which is a sleeping lock on PREEMPT_RT;
it does not request a raw lock.

Set use_raw_spinlock so the owner publishes the non-sleeping map needed
by the voltage transaction. Preserve the register allowlists, setup
ordering, permanent ownership and publication checks. The PMIC parent
map used by the same transaction requires the separate companion fix.

The actual regmap selection and callbacks reproduce18 failed checks
across the two old configurations; fixing only the L2 map leaves9.
Both corrected configurations pass20 cases/149 checks, with two failing
controls. The original L2 publication and no-voltage-write model passes.
Four native ARM/ARM64 profiles, with and without PREEMPT_RT, compile
24 related objects with W=1 and no diagnostics. Lock services and IPI
context are synthetic; physical RT/lockdep acceptance is still pending.

Codex generated this fix and qualification. Human review and DCO remain
pending; no Signed-off-by is added.

Fixes: b920df1379ab ("soc: qcom: spm: initialize the MSM8226 L2 arbiter master")

commits.author: Codex
commits.original_message:
mfd: qcom-spmi-pmic: use a raw lock for atomic register access

The SPMI PMIC map advertises fast_io and is accessed by the SAW voltage
callback from a synchronous CPU0 IPI. Its spinlock_t becomes a sleeping
lock on PREEMPT_RT, so the PMIC access has an invalid wait context even
when the SAW MMIO map itself uses a raw lock.

Request a raw spinlock for the parent map. Keep the existing fast-I/O
allocation policy and serialize all children through the same map.
The SPMI register transport and PMIC arbiter callbacks remain unchanged.

Executing the actual regmap selection and lock callbacks detects the
regular lock and synthetic invalid IPI wait. The corrected L2 and PMIC
maps pass20 cases/149 checks, while both deliberately broken controls
fail. Native ARM and ARM64 PREEMPT_RT profiles on this fresh MFD base
compile10 related objects with W=1 and no diagnostics. Four combined
ARM/ARM64 RT and ordinary profiles also compile24 objects cleanly.
This is source/model qualification; no physical RT/lockdep trial ran.

Codex generated this fix and qualification. Human review and DCO remain
pending; no Signed-off-by is added.

Fixes: c3a973a770a1 ("mfd: Add support for Qualcomm SPMI PMICs")

commits.original_message:
regulator: qcom-spmi: retain current SAW mapping APIs in the runtime

Integrate the qualified standalone regulator port fa4d0bf7b86d onto the
combined runtime, preserving its complete fixed-range APC policy.
Only the permanent MSM8226 L2 master uses its published shared map;
legacy SAWs keep private raw-lock MMIO maps and errors stop probe.
Select REGMAP_MMIO for the driver's direct mapping dependency.

These bytes retain Dmitry Baryshkov's 053c50a70525 upstream raw-map fix
and Kees Cook's 4dd10fbbeb9c allocator API conversion from the pinned
regulator for-next base. Timothy Schmidt's fixed-range feature algorithm
and original attribution remain in the preceding source history. Codex
performed the current-base mapping split, integration and qualification.

The standalone source passes two native RT profiles, three actual
FTS2/provider/recovery methods, the 47-case/407-check acquisition model
and four rejected controls. The separate L2 and PMIC raw-lock fixes are
retained. Full package reproducibility, physical RT/lockdep, voltage and
power acceptance remain separate. Human review/DCO are pending; no
Signed-off-by is added.
